pages.title: The Charter
pages.text: Bureaucratic. Slow. Generous. Legalistic.$(br2)Those four words are how every senior Foreman describes the Charter when pressed. None of them are wrong.

The Charter's strength is its $(l)patience$(). It will sign almost any reasonable docket, given time and tea. Its weakness is the same. A claim filed today may not be audited for a year. A complaint filed today may never be heard.$(br2)Foremen learn to keep their own books clean. The Charter audits eventually.

The Charter is $(o)not$() a military body. It has clerks and surveyors and the occasional auditor. It does not have armies. When pirates raid a colony, the Charter writes a strongly worded note and dispatches a survey ship to count the dead.$(br2)Some Foremen find this comforting. Some do not.
